item: A29 remediation — federated playback, dereferenceable ids, social parity
verdict: NOT FLIPPED — code remediation only; the two-instance re-run is a later slice
section: A29 remediation — federated playback, dereferenceable ids, social parity — 2026-09-08
headline: The three failing clauses of INT-05, the four findings the row recorded without letting them decide it, and the three the evidence file carried beyond the row now have code behind them, proved by unit and integration tests with the migrations APPLIED to a real PostgreSQL 16.15. What did not run is the part the verdict turns on: no second instance, no caching edge, no running Caddy, no browser pointed at a live backend.

prs.ordering: core first; vidra-user regenerates lib/api/generated.ts from core's openapi.yaml and stays a DRAFT until core#203 merges, because contract-ci compares against core main

migrations.0139_federation_delivery_identity: request_id/correlation_id on federation_deliveries + a second trigger carrying them onto the job_runs row the 0083 projection creates
migrations.numbering: 0137 belonged to the A33 purge-jobs slice, which merged during this one; the branch was rebased onto it and the sequence is contiguous
migrations.applied: migrate up from an empty database reached version 140 clean on PostgreSQL 16.15 — applied, not merely linted
migrations.0140_remote_video_comments: the MIRRORED comment thread on a remote video — a separate table, not a nullable comments.video_id, and deliberately with no user_id column

cors_matrix.rule: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * exactly when the response is PUBLIC (the route's own Eligible assertion) AND NON-CREDENTIALED (no ?pt=, no Authorization, no video-read cookie in use)
cors_matrix.seam: every place delivery.CacheControl is applied and nowhere else: serveMediaAsset's api-proxy branch, setHLSCacheControl, setMediaCacheControl
wildcard: public HLS master and variant playlists
avatars, banners, playlist covers, instance logos
the CDN edge's own origin fetch of a public object
no_header: the edge's origin fetch of a non-public object

preflight.mechanism: mediaPreflight runs BEFORE echo's CORS middleware and PRE-SEEDS the wildcard answer; the middleware overwrites it with the credentialed answer for an allow-listed Origin and leaves it in place otherwise — echo terminates every preflight itself, so a route-level answer is unreachable
preflight.why_needed: hls.js sends Range on CMAF byte ranges, which is not CORS-safelisted; A32 measured zero preflights only because those fetches were same-origin

cors_matrix.vary_origin: not added — the value is a constant, not a reflection of the request's Origin. Echo's CORS middleware adds one of its own to every response, pre-existing and untouched.

outbound_video.id: https://<origin>/videos/<uuid> — FROZEN; moving it re-identifies the video on every peer
outbound_video.url: an ARRAY of Links: the HLS master as application/x-mpegURL, then the /v/<code> watch page as text/html
outbound_video.icon: an Image object carrying mediaType; width/height OMITTED because vidra records the video's dimensions, never the poster's
outbound_video.duration: xsd:duration whole seconds (PT367S), the form PeerTube emits and parseISODurationSeconds reads
outbound_video.omission_rule: every field is omitted when the fact behind it is absent — no ladder means no stream link, no poster means no icon, no probe means no duration
outbound_video.create_vs_update: the publish hook fires Create, which for every video that is not publish_after_transcode is BEFORE the transcode finishes. The transcode completion hook now fires UpdateVideo LAST — after releaseHold, because UpdateVideo reads the video's CURRENT privacy/state and would otherwise skip or unfederate it. composeTranscodeCompletion pins the order [release, mirror, federate].
outbound_video.proof: a REAL emitted activity is driven through the REAL ingest parsers (videoLinks/iconURL/parseISODurationSeconds), and the outbox object is asserted byte-identical to the delivered one

negotiation_rules.ap_answer: 200 with the AS object, ETag over the serialised bytes, Cache-Control: public, max-age=300
negotiation_rules.other_accept: 406 — core has no HTML, exactly as the actor and collection routes already answer
negotiation_rules.non_public: 404, identical to a uuid that was never a video, so the endpoint is not an enumeration oracle
negotiation_rules.deleted: 410 + Tombstone (id, formerType, deleted), Cache-Control: no-store — never cached, because a 410 can legitimately become a 200 again after a restore
negotiation_rules.federated_note: 404 — a federated comment's id belongs to its origin; re-serving it under our own URL would mint a second identity for one object
negotiation_rules.routing: deploy/Caddyfile content-negotiates /videos/* and /comments/* to the api on an AP Accept; a browser never matches (no activity+json or ld+json in a browser's Accept) and the api answers 406 anyway. NOT exercised against a running Caddy in this slice.
negotiation_rules.signed_fetch: NOT implemented — recorded as a follow-up. The objects are public by construction so nothing leaks, but a peer requiring signed dereferencing is not served, and vidra sends no signature on its own object fetches.

findings.note: icon, duration and an HLS url on the outbound Video; an Update when the transcode lands; CORS on public media so the link is usable
core handlers for /videos/{uuid} and /comments/{uuid} plus the Caddy Accept rule
ResolveSearchTarget consults remote_videos by object id OR watch url before any fetch

a federation.inbox.rejected audit row now records the refusal (the 202 is deliberately unchanged — a distinguishable refusal is a probe target). REDELIVERY after an unblock is still not attempted and stays OPEN.
an Undo or Reject bound for a blocked destination is delivered rather than cancelled — a block is a refusal to receive, and swallowing the one message that reduces contact makes it leakier
CountChannelFollowers is local + accepted remote, one definition, read by the AP collection too
remote_actor_blocks + GET/POST/DELETE /me/blocks/remote + a Settings tab; feeds, inbound Notes and inbound Follows all honour it

findings.status: fixed for the direction A29 measured; authoring deferred
findings.note: migration 0140 mirrors the thread the origin already fans out to us, and the follower's page shows it. The authority rule has three checks and the third is specific to this path: the Note's origin must be the VIDEO's origin, or any instance in our follow graph could write onto any mirrored video from any other instance. AUTHORING against a remote video stays deferred: it reverses a shipped product decision (comments, ratings and saving live on the origin instance), raises the question of who answers for a comment an instance hosts about a video it does not own, and would need an account-level follower collection that A29-F11 says does not exist. There is no user_id column and no POST, deliberately.
410 + Tombstone from federated_video_tombstones, written by the same delete path that fans the Delete out, BEFORE the fan-out so an AP-disabled or vanished channel still answers
request/correlation identity on the delivery queue row and onto job_runs; a federation component on /admin/system
account actor collections stay hard-coded empty — a documented decision in collections.go, unchanged by this slice
urlsafety.Guard runs on EVERY actor resolution, cached or not; a signature failing against the cached key is retried once against a freshly fetched one, bounded to actors already cached

admin_federation_component.degraded: dead_lettered > 0 — a peer refusing our activities is not this instance being down, and the overall verdict stays ok
admin_federation_component.down: the oldest PENDING delivery older than 20 minutes — the full ladder (30s doubling to attempt 6, about 15.5 minutes) plus a drain interval, so a queue walking its backoff is never called stalled
admin_federation_component.absent: when federation is not wired — an instance that does not federate has no federation health

remote_account_block.keyed_on: the ACTOR URL, not a remote_actors FK — a viewer must be able to block an actor never cached here, and evicting the cache must not lift a block
effects: the blocker's feeds and reads exclude that actor's remote videos
an inbound Create{Note} on a video the BLOCKER owns is dropped
an inbound Follow of a channel the BLOCKER owns records nothing and sends nothing
deliberately_not: it does not hide the blocker from the blocked actor
remote_account_block.why_not: a remote server decides what it shows its own users; a safety feature that only reads as protection is the worst kind
remote_account_block.unblock: matches the stored URL VERBATIM — no handle resolution, so a WebFinger that has since started failing cannot strand a viewer with an unliftable block

vidra-core.make ci: PASS (fmt-check, vet, migrate-lint 140 up migrations clean, openapi-verify, sqlc-verify, test-race)
vidra-core.integration: ok on a fresh PostgreSQL 16.15 for internal/federation, internal/store and internal/httpapi, run per package — internal/store's owner-claim test needs an empty users table and fails after the federation suite has seeded one, on this branch and on clean main alike

vidra-user.node: 22 locally, NOT the Node 26 CI uses
vidra-user.e2e: the MOCKED Playwright suite ran: 627 specs, all passing on a clean re-run. player-theater.spec.ts failed once under full-suite load and passes in isolation — the known flake. It caught the one real defect in this slice's frontend half: e2e/remote-videos.spec.ts pinned the old info-panel copy. The BACKED suites were not run locally.

meta.python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p: see the run recorded with this section
meta.scripts: no script changed — only deploy/Caddyfile and docs

not_run: a running Caddy against the new content-negotiation rule
the mirrored thread against a second live instance — the exact delivery A29 watched succeed into a drop
the BACKED Playwright suites (they build vidra-core from its default branch, which does not yet carry this slice's endpoints)
open: A29-F4: an activity refused during an instance block is still never redelivered after the unblock
A29-F8's AUTHORING half: a comment written HERE about a remote video. It reverses a shipped product decision and needs a moderation ruling; the mirroring half is built.
A29-F11: account actor collections stay hard-coded empty, which is also why a comment authored here would have no follower set to fan out to
signed fetch on the AP object routes, in both directions
QoE for remote playback is deliberately not emitted; whether a viewer's own instance should measure playback it did not serve is a product question
